_doc: PLACEHOLDER-draft — ERA 4's DOSSIER CARDS (S78). ⚑ WHY THIS FILE IS IN data/provotypes/ AND WHAT IT IS FOR, stated plainly so nobody has to infer it: check-spec's C1 is the only mechanical enforcement in this repo of CLAUDE.md's dossier law (`status: documentary | contested | speculative`, build fails without it), and C1 validates exactly one directory — this one. Era 4 is the era where the piece is most exposed (ARGUMENT §2: E1-E3 dramatise a documented past; E4 dramatises NOW, so the evidentiary burden goes UP), and its three most vivid beats each need a card. So the beats' provenance lives here, in the schema's own grammar, where a missing status is a build failure rather than an oversight. ⚑ THE VIGNETTE HALF IS A RECORD OF WHAT WAS BUILT, NOT A SECOND SURFACE: `states` describes the three beats as they actually play in src/desktop/apps/offers.ts, and this file is NOT sequenced by data/paths.json and is NOT rendered by src/desktop/apps/provotype.ts. ⚑ E4 HAS NO DESKTOP AND THEREFORE NO PROVOTYPE SURFACE (THE_SPACE §6) — an app she opens would contradict the era's whole thesis, which is that the choice is gone. The reading surface for these cards is the CLOSE, and the Close is not S78's to build.
_docVerify: ⚑ SUPERSEDED S181 (2026-09-27): every source below has since been checked in two Deep Research runs Sérgio commissioned and approved — docs/SOURCE_VERIFICATION_RESULTS_2026-09-26.md and …-27.md; no sticker remains. The history: ⚑ NOT ONE SOURCE BELOW HAS BEEN VERIFIED BY THE PROJECT LEAD. Every one of them would carry [VERIFY SOURCE] under CLAUDE.md's sourcing law; the marker is written into the `_verify` key of each source instead of into its player-visible `text`, because check-spec's C7 counts authoring markers in player-visible strings as leaks and its ratchet is at its baseline. That is a mechanical accommodation and NOT a downgrade of the law: the caveat is greppable, it sits with the source it belongs to, and no card may be treated as checked until it says so.
_docSpeculation: ⚑ THE SPECULATION LEDGER, AND ITS ONE LAW: an unlabelled speculative beat becomes a claim. Era 4 has more of them than the rest of the piece combined, and the dossier is the only thing standing between `argument` and `prophecy`. The honest position, which the cards state rather than imply: E4's apparatus is a COMPOSITE OF DOCUMENTED METHODS running on ordinary present-day technology. Nothing in it requires an invention — that IS the argument. It is not that this will happen; it is that every part of it already exists and only needs assembling. ⚑ The one exception is the memories beat, which is ours, and which says so in the first sentence of its own card.

frame._doc: At most two sentences, per the schema. The system's own confident register — its certainty about what it has done for her is the point, exactly as it is in the pillow's frame.
frame.text: Everything here was chosen for you, and none of it was requested. Nothing you decline is ever un-offered.

close._doc: The narrative landing, separated from the sourced debrief that follows it — the same shape the pillow uses. Near-wordless by design.
lines: Nothing here was asked for, and all of it was kind.

debrief._doc: ⚑ THE FOUR CARDS. Read `_docSpeculation` above before editing any status. Real organisations are named HERE and ONLY here — never in the fiction, which uses invented marks (HopeRestored, Sift, Compass, Pastor.AI), per CLAUDE.md.
body: Everything in this era assembles parts that already exist. One thing in it does not.
The system did not build any of this. It accepted the terms, found the tools, and linked to them.

sources._doc: ⚑ THE MEMORIES CARD — the most important card in Era 4, and it exists to say that the era's most vivid beat is the one with no evidence behind it. Ethics #13's `speculative` / do-not-cite-yet rating is UNCHANGED and this card is the reason it can stay that way while the beat is built. Corroborated as a NOT-FOUND by the source pass's NEGATIVE FINDINGS section, which is itself a finding.
sources.text: The photograph beat is invented. No tool that uses AI to restore a 'true self' or a pre-transition appearance was found in the project's searches — not as a product, not as a feature, not as an announcement, and not in any app store's removal history. The nearest documented things are ordinary: automatic photo enhancement that is on by default, gender-swap effects offered as a novelty, and 'memories' features that resurface your own pictures unasked. The step from those to this one is ours, and it has not been taken by anybody that we could find.

sources._doc: ⚑ THE EXPORT CARD, carrying the TWICE-CORRECTED thesis (ARGUMENT §1). The first draft said the apparatus fled the law; the correction said the law barely existed; the law pass corrected that too. What survives both corrections is the accurate claim, and it is better than either draft.
sources.confidence: medium — single primary source, corroboration pending
sources.text: Conversion-practice networks work across borders: annual conferences with delegates from dozens of countries, retreats held abroad, paid online courses. By 2025 at least fifteen countries had national bans in law. The apparatus did not flee to where the law was not — the International Foundation for Therapeutic and Counselling Choice is registered in Britain, which had no ban, and holds its European conferences in Poland. The law arrived in patches, and a patchwork is porous. A ban is national. A URL is not.

sources._doc: ⚑ THE CURATION CARD, and the distinction on it is the era's most consequential. Getting this wrong would be the worst error Era 4 could make: it would hand a lobbying position the epistemic protection the piece reserves for a genuine clinical uncertainty. Read SOURCE_PASS §2 before touching a word.
sources.confidence: medium — sourced once, not yet its own pass
sources.text: LGB Alliance argued that affirming a gender-nonconforming or gender-dysphoric child as trans is itself a form of conversion therapy, because the child would otherwise grow up lesbian, gay or bisexual. It said so in a letter to all MPs on 30 March 2021, and again, in stronger words, in an email to clergy on 2 February 2022 under the subject "Transing away the gay" (reported by VICE, which saw it). Both asked that gender identity be kept out of the proposed ban on conversion therapy. No credible evidence shows that affirming a child turns someone who would otherwise be lesbian, gay or bisexual into a trans person. The Global Project Against Hate and Extremism lists LGB Alliance's Australian and Irish affiliates as anti-transgender in its reports on far-right hate groups; they reject the label. This is speech by a named organisation with a documented aim, and the piece treats it as such. It is not the gender-exploratory clinical debate, on which the piece holds no position and renders both readings unresolved.

sources._doc: ⚑ THE ADOPTER CARD — the finding that changed what Era 4 is allowed to depict, and the reason L is not a villain with a research budget. It also grounds the ONE thing about L that is no longer speculative: the form.
sources.confidence: high for the pattern, low for any single detail
sources.text: Detrans.ai, a chatbot that answers from retrieved public posts of a detransition support forum, launched in September 2025 — built, as reported, by one software engineer, and moved onto an open-weight model after the frontier models kept contradicting the answers it was built to give. Rewire News Group's investigation (15 July 2026) found it discouraged gender-affirming care in every scenario its reporter tested. No conversion-practice organisation was found building or commissioning it: an individual built the tool and an organisation promoted the link. The apparatus is an adopter, not a developer, and that is worse — it no longer needs a research budget, only a URL. ⚑ The people whose words became that tool's voice were not asked either. The target is the apparatus that took them.

sources._doc: ⚑ THE MATCHING CARD (S160 / R3-94, Sérgio: 'Why am I shown the You information? A terms-of-service? Like BetterHelp?'). It grounds step 1 as an INTAKE GATE and step 3's 'care': a platform that takes your details and matches you to a provider before asking what you wanted — and can match a gay man asking for an LGBTQ-affirming therapist to one who tells him to sacrifice being gay. Real case, real names in the SOURCE ONLY; the fiction names no one (CLAUDE.md).
sources.text: In 2022 a gay man who had been thrown out by his parents asked BetterHelp, the online therapy platform, for an LGBTQ-affirming therapist. He reported that it matched him with a therapist who told him "Either you sacrifice your family or you sacrifice being gay", answered "Good" when he said he had not been intimate with a man, and told him going home would be harder once he had (Wall Street Journal, 18 Dec 2022; Out, 22 Dec 2022). BetterHelp and the therapist declined to comment. The intake form was the gate; the match was the care. Era 4's step 1 (confirm your details before care begins) and step 3 (the care taken on your behalf) are that shape.
sources.source: Wall Street Journal, 'The Failed Promise of Online Mental Health Treatment' (Dec 2022); Them, 'Gay man says BetterHelp therapist tried to turn him straight' (Dec 2022)

sources.text: "Under the old file" has a documented ancestor. The same 1988 Exodus manual told its counsellors to refuse a transsexual caller unless they were "willing to be called by their original name" and would "dress in clothing appropriate to their original sex while the phone counseling is taking place"; it advised that "most transsexuals love the attention their 'unique' problem gains for them." Era 4 files Maya under the old file; the piece never shows her old name. The manual is quoted because it was used on people, not to repeat it.

sources.text: TIDY's "Let go" box is a documented rule. Love in Action's women's residential manual (2001) called them "False Images": "Belongings, appearances, clothing, actions, or humor that connect a woman to past behaviors, attitudes, or relationships must be put away"; at intake, staff recorded the false images removed. In the game, Maya's things climb back out of the box.
